api.unknown: An unknown error occurred while processing request.
api.unauthorized: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.

auth.callbackError: An error occurred while completing the sign-in. Please try again.

register.title: Register
register.description: Enter your invitation code to create an account.

collection.capabilitiesFailed: The filters of this list could not be read. The records below are complete.

required.help: A claim the person must have a value for before the flow lets them back to the application, collected rather than left for a client to ask for later. See {link} for details.

identifier.help: An identifier claim is one of the values a person signs in with — an email address, a username, an employee number. A value belongs to one account across the whole set of them, and a provider asserting one is how a third-party sign-in reaches the account that already holds it rather than opening a second. See {link} for details.

type.help: A client is an application that delegates the sign-in of its users to this server. A confidential client can keep a secret, and authenticates with a client id and a secret — a server-side application, a backend job. A public client cannot, because its code runs where the person can read it — a single-page application, a mobile app — so it authenticates with its client id alone. See {link} for details.

registrationMode.label: Registration mode
registrationMode.help: How somebody comes by an account in this audience. Open lets anybody sign up, invitation-only closes sign-up to everybody holding no invitation, open + invitations allows either, and closed leaves the Admin API as the only way an account is created. See {link} for details.

values.oauth2_authorize: Signing in at a client's request

logoutDialog.title: Force Logout
logoutDialog.description: Revoke authentication tokens for this user. They will need to sign in again.

noAccess.title: No access
noAccess.description: You are signed in as {account}, but the token this console was issued opens none of its pages.
noAccess.scopes: Ask an administrator to grant one of these:

users.title: Users

status.label: Status
status.help: An account is one person this server authenticates and holds the claims of. A disabled one is refused when it signs in with a password, and told what somebody typing the wrong password is told; it keeps everything it holds, since disabling an account deletes nothing of it. See {link} for details.

users.identifierClaimsFailed: The configured claims could not be read, so the columns naming each account are missing. The accounts below are complete.

userDetail.title: User
userDetail.enrollMfaDescription: Generate a link that lets this user enroll a multi-factor authentication method. Once they complete enrollment they are returned to the selected client's URL.
userDetail.enrollMfaNoRedirectUris: This client has no registered redirect URIs. Choose another client or add a redirect URI to it first.
userDetail.enrollMfaLinkWarning: Hand or send this link to the user. Following it lets them enroll an MFA method, then returns them to the selected return URL.
userDetail.linkProviderDescription: Generate a link that lets this user link an external identity provider to their account. They must confirm the request, re-authenticate, then authorize the provider before the link is created. Once done they are returned to the selected client's URL.
userDetail.linkProviderProviderIdHelp: Identifier of the provider to link, as configured on the server.
userDetail.linkProviderNoRedirectUris: This client has no registered redirect URIs. Choose another client or add a redirect URI to it first.
userDetail.linkProviderLinkWarning: Hand or send this link to the user. Following it lets them confirm, re-authenticate, and authorize the provider to link it to their account, then returns them to the selected return URL.

type.label: Type
type.help: A scope is a named permission a client asks for, and that this server records in the token it issues. A consentable scope protects the person's claims and nothing but their consent grants it; a grantable one protects a resource and this deployment's granting rules decide it rather than the person; a client scope belongs to the client itself and needs no person at all. See {link} for details.

origin.help: Who defined the scope: the OAuth 2 or OpenID Connect specifications, SympAuthy itself, or this deployment's configuration. A scope of your own is asked for, granted and carried exactly like a standard one. See {link} for details.

claims.label: Claims
claims.help: The claims a client may read once the person has consented to this scope. Only a consentable scope protects claims, so every other kind lists none. See {link} for details.

audienceId.label: Audience ID
audienceId.help: An audience is a group of clients sharing one pool of the person's consents: a consent given through any of them covers them all, and every token issued for one names the audience in its aud claim. A client belongs to exactly one. See {link} for details.

invitations.title: Invitations

status.label: Status
status.help: Where the invitation stands. A pending one is still usable; a consumed one was signed up with and cannot be used twice; a revoked one an operator cancelled; an expired one ran out of time before anybody used it.

tokenPrefix.label: Token prefix
tokenPrefix.help: An invitation is a single-use token somebody signs up with — how a person registers where the audience lets nobody sign up on their own, and a way to assign claims to the account up front where it does. This is the start of that token, which is all this server keeps of it: the whole of it is answered once, when the invitation is created, and never again. See {link} for details.

invitations.revokeDescription: This invitation will no longer be usable. This action cannot be undone.

claims.label: Claims (JSON)
claims.help: Claims written onto the account the moment somebody registers with this invitation, as a JSON object of claim ids and values. Only a claim of this deployment's own is accepted: a standard one such as email or name has to come from the person themselves. A granting rule reading such a claim is how an invitation comes to grant scopes. See {link} for details.

invitations.invalidJson: Claims must be a valid JSON object.
invitations.tokenWarning: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again.
invitations.search: Search by token prefix or note

kind.label: Kind
kind.help: Whose the claim's value is, which decides who may write it. A personal claim is the person's: collected from them, and disclosed to a client once they agreed to a scope. An application claim is a backend's, attached to the person, and never typed by them. A claim this server computes itself is of neither kind and carries none. See {link} for details.

origin.help: Who named the claim: the OpenID Connect specification, or this deployment itself. A name of either kind says nothing about whose the value is or who may read it — a client is told a claim of your own exactly like a standard one. See {link} for details.

publishedIn.label: Published in
publishedIn.help: Where the claim's value travels once it leaves this server: the ID token, the userinfo response, the access token and the introspection response each carry it. The discovery document advertises the claim's name alone, so a client learns the claim exists without being told anybody's value. A claim published nowhere is carried by no token and stays readable through this panel. See {link} for details.

sessions.title: Sessions

status.label: Status
status.help: A session is one person's trip through this server's own pages — signing in for an application, enrolling a second factor, confirming an action. An ongoing one is still in flight; completed, cancelled, failed and expired are what it ended as, and an expired one is a trip the person simply stopped. See {link} for details.

user.label: User
user.help: Who the session has identified, which is nobody until the person has authenticated. One creating the account it will belong to reads as signing up, and one that has identified nobody at all carries a dash.

sessions.search: Search by IP, user agent or client
sessions.empty: No interactive flow session is in flight. This is a live view rather than a history — expired sessions are collected every fifteen minutes, so a session that has finished may already be gone.

sessionDetail.title: Session
sessionDetail.notFound: This session no longer exists. It may have completed and been collected — expired sessions are collected every fifteen minutes.

userClaims.title: Claims
userClaims.help: A claim is a piece of information this server holds about a person — their name, their email address, a tier a backend computed. These are the values this account holds, with when each was collected and whether it has been verified. See {link} for details.

userConsents.title: Consents
userConsents.help: A consent is the person's agreement to disclose some of their claims to an audience, given in the flow when a client asked for a scope. Every client of that audience reads it, and revoking it asks the person again the next time one of them needs the scope. See {link} for details.

userMfa.title: MFA Methods
userMfa.help: Multi-factor authentication methods registered by this user. Revoking a method will require the user to set it up again. See {link} for details.
userMfa.revokeDescription: This will remove the MFA method from the user's account. They will need to set it up again.

userProviders.title: Provider Links
userProviders.help: External identity providers linked to this user's account. Unlinking a provider will prevent the user from signing in with it. See {link} for details.
userProviders.subject: Subject
userProviders.unlinkDescription: This will remove the link between this user and the identity provider. The user will no longer be able to sign in with this provider.

sessionSecurityContexts.title: Security contexts
sessionSecurityContexts.help: A security context is a place a session was driven from: one address, one user agent, and where the edge in front of this server says that address is. One entry per place, counting the requests that came from each rather than repeating them. Only a place where a credential was actually proven carries a proven date — anybody holding the session's state can produce the others. The list is bounded: once it is full, a request from a new place rolls out the one seen least recently, and a proven place is the last to go. See {link} for details.
sessionSecurityContexts.empty: Nothing was recorded against this session. Recording is best-effort and never fails a flow, so a session may hold no place at all.
sessionSecurityContexts.search: Search by address, user agent or place

sessionPurposes.title: Purposes
sessionPurposes.help: A purpose is something a flow can only settle with the person in front of a browser: signing in for an application, enrolling a second factor, confirming an action. One card per purpose this session carries, in the order it drives them, each labelled as the server wrote it rather than in this panel's language. See {link} for details.
sessionPurposes.noDebugInformation: This purpose has nothing to say about the session.

sessionFailure.title: Failure
sessionFailure.help: What the session ended with, offered by one that failed and by one its expiry ended — nothing refused an expired session, the person simply stopped, and the flow told them so all the same. Every field below explains itself. See {link} for details.
sessionFailure.notFailed: This session has not ended in a failure. It carries nothing to read here.
sessionFailure.nothingRecorded: This session ended in a failure the server recorded nothing about — no code, no message, no values. Its status is all there is to read of it.

errorDetailsId.label: Internal error code
errorDetailsId.help: The key the server failed this session under. It is the contract and outlives any rewording of the two messages below, so it is what you search the server's error messages for, what you quote in a bug report, and what a console groups failures by.

errorDetails.label: Internal error message
errorDetails.help: What the code means, written for whoever operates this server and read in this panel's language. It may name a row, a claim, a provider or a key, and the person in the flow was never shown it. Empty where this deployment holds no message under the code.

errorDescription.label: User-facing error message
errorDescription.help: The sentence the flow's error page actually put on the person's screen. A failure naming no message of its own falls back to the generic one, so this is what they were told rather than what the failure asked for — which is the sentence to expect them to quote back to you.

values.label: Additional values
values.help: What the server interpolated into the two messages, published raw as well so each can be read on its own — the address that was refused, the scope that was not granted. They arrive whether or not either message did, so these may be all this failure has to say. The keys are the server's own and differ from one failure to the next.
